statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 6 of 100 in the low band, nineteen points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME weekend closure removes the very price path this score measures. Stress stays at 52 in the elevated band: Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, the Hormuz bypass carrying 4-5% of global supply, remains shut after Thursday's drone strikes with no published repair timeline, and Houthi forces completed their grip on Bab el-Mandeb by taking Perim island, Mocha and Dhubab. Confidence is 86: levels, yields, crude, VIX, the catalyst stack and the seven-day calendar were all re-verified against primary sources this hour, while no live price path exists to observe.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and the single shared reading applies to both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Three observations support it. First, Friday's completed path granted mean reversion rather than denying it: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, about 105 points below its 29,473.12 high inside a 159.61-point cash range, and VIX fell 11.21% to 15.84. Second, CME equity index futures have been halted since 21:00 UTC Friday and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC Sunday, about three hours after the final slot of this horizon closes, so no slot contains a tradeable session and no danger window is published. Third, a supply-channel constraint is not a price path: the Bab el-Mandeb seizure and the pipeline outage belong in Stress until a live session shows persistent one-way Nasdaq structure. Stress holds at 52 because triple-digit crude, a 4.95% ten-year, the shut pipeline and a contested 16 September FOMC decision are all unresolved into next week. Stress alone does not change the mapped state.
headline: Twenty-two hours into the CME weekend halt the Nasdaq-100 still stands at its 29,368.44 Friday close with VIX 15.84 and WTI marked $100.05, while Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline stays shut with no repair timeline and Houthi forces hold Bab el-Mandeb; market pricing for Wednesday's FOMC leans to a 25 basis point increase near 56% on CME FedWatch without being decisive.
body:
The price picture is unchanged, as expected across a closed weekend, and was re-verified against primary sources this hour. The Nasdaq-100 quote page shows a 29,368.44 close, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close, so the cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished about 105 points below the high, roughly 4.5% under the 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. VIX is 15.84, down 11.21% from 17.84, having settled near the 15.59 low of a 15.59 to 17.71 range. The latest H.15 observation, for 10 September, shows the 2-year at 4.56%, the 10-year at 4.95% and the 30-year at 5.37%. WTI is marked $100.05, down 2.37% on the day but up 9.7% on the week and 20.15% on the month, with Brent $104.61, down 2.81%.

Friday's session was the first advance after four consecutive declines, and it came on a mixed inflation print rather than a clean one. August CPI rose 0.4% on the month and 3.4% over the year, with gasoline up 3.9% on the month and 27.4% on the year; core CPI rose 0.3%, a tenth above forecast, while the core annual rate eased to 2.4%. Equities rallied anyway as crude gave back part of the week's gain. That combination is why the forward risk sits in Stress rather than Tail: the completed path was two-sided and closed below its high.

The unresolved set is the supply channel and the policy decision. Saudi Arabia's 745-mile East-West pipeline, which moves between 4% and 5% of global oil supplies and serves as the bypass around the blocked Strait of Hormuz, was shut after Thursday's drone strikes; the energy ministry described precautionary measures and published no repair timeline, and Riyadh agreed not to retaliate immediately at Iraq's request after an Iraqi commander was dismissed. Houthi forces took Perim island, Mocha and Dhubab to complete effective control of the Bab el-Mandeb gateway serving Yanbu, and the IEA reported Saudi crude supply at its lowest in more than three decades. Against that, President Trump said on 9 September that the war would end immediately after the 3 November midterms, and Iran-Oman talks on a shared Hormuz route are reported to be close to a signing.

Next week supplies the scheduled catalysts. Retail Sales and the FOMC decision with projections both land on 16 September, followed by the Chair's press conference; CME FedWatch put a 25 basis point increase near 56% after the Jackson Hole remarks, with Kalshi and Polymarket nearer 48-49%, so the decision is genuinely contested. The index also faces its own mechanics, with SpaceX's weighting set to rise and roughly $15.5 billion of estimated passive buying around the 18 September close. Shared Finviz context collected at 18:49 UTC corroborates Friday's tone as delayed latest-session evidence only: NQ +0.86%, VIX futures -8.41%, crude -2.37%, seven of eight megacaps higher and semiconductors averaging +1.75%, with Treasury futures modestly lower. None of that is live price-path evidence, and none of it is treated as such here.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 19:00 UTC on 11 September to 18:00 UTC on 12 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens in the U.S. afternoon that followed Friday's CPI print, with Tail at 17 then 13 in mixed mode and Stress in the high band near 77 decaying as the event passed and volatility fell. Tail dropped to 7 at the 21:00 UTC futures halt and has since held a 5 to 6 band in normal mode across the final twenty-one slots, tracking the closure rather than any directional view. Stress fell from 77 to 50 before ticking back to 52 on the verified Red Sea escalation, and Confidence held inside the high band throughout, between 85 and 89. No slot in the window reached the 25-point Tail block threshold.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forward slots lies inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday, and the reference contract does not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, about three hours after this horizon's final slot closes. Conditional Tail opens at 6 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical structure, then steps gradually to a ceiling of 15 as unpriced weekend headline exposure accumulates ahead of the reopen. Every slot stays inside the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and green throughout, and no danger window is published because no slot contains a tradeable session. Stress runs from 52 down to a floor of 48 through the overnight quiet, then climbs to 54 as the Sunday Gulf session, a reported Monday Muscat signing on a shared Hormuz route and the reopen approach with their outcomes unknown. Mode stays normal until the final three slots, where it becomes mixed to reflect a genuinely two-sided conditional gap distribution. Confidence decays from 86 to 80 purely as a function of distance from the last verified market observation. The conditions that would change this picture are observable only after the reopen: an opening gap that refuses retracement, repeated extension after failed pullbacks, or an energy-led repricing that cross-assets confirm.
